messages:
Sam: Quick share from the seq-len sweep I ran last night across L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. Wanted to capture the surprising kernel routing behaviour and a proposed small preset to reduce tail latency.

Priya: Nice. main takeaway first? numbers or TL;DR? :eyes:

Sam: TL;DR: for seq<=64 and batch<=2, our current default kernel pick (large-matmul-tiling) on L4/T4/A10 gives ~20-35% lower p95 latency than on A100/H100 because of launch & padding overheads. For seq>=512 A100/H100 wins as expected. Also KV cache warmup pattern differs — small GPUs show faster first-token latency when cache is cold.

Miguel: Interesting — do you have the profiling traces? nvprof/NSight or runtime counters?

Sam: Posted snippets below. Captured: kernel name, launch_us, sm_efficiency, gld_gst throughput (GB/s). Example (seq=32, batch=1):
```
L4: triton_attn_small_seq kernel - launch 120us, exec 310us, sm_eff 42%, gld 85GB/s
A100: triton_attn_big_batch kernel - launch 220us, exec 410us, sm_eff 58%, gld 240GB/s
```
Notice that L4 kernel has lower absolute exec time for this config because it avoids big GEMM padding.

Elena: That matches what I saw in the microbenchmarks — for short sequences the effective compute/IO ratio shifts and our big-kernel heuristics overpad leading to wasted work on H100/A100.

Priya: Where does KV cache fit in? We always assumed bigger GPUs warm KV faster due to bandwidth.

Sam: Right. For cold KV we measured first-token-only latency (fetch + attn): L4 was 18% faster at seq=16 because its small-kernel path keeps less temporary state and fewer kernel launches. However, sustained throughput after cache warm favors A100/H100 massively. So we should route by seqlen+cache-state.

Miguel: Can we codify this into a runtime preset? Something like: if seq<=64 and batch<=4 prefer small-fused kernels on L4/T4/A10; else prefer big-tiling kernels and tensor-optimized paths on A100/H100.

Sam: Exactly. Proposed preset (pseudo-config):
```
"kernel_presets": [
  {"arch_regex": "(l4|t4|a10)", "seq_max": 64, "batch_max": 4, "kernel_family": "triton_small_fused", "priority": 10},
  {"arch_regex": "(a100|h100)", "seq_min": 65, "kernel_family": "tensor_large_tiling", "priority": 5},
  {"default": true, "kernel_family": "balanced_dynamic"}
]
```
This is just a local heuristic; runtime should still fallback if memory/SM occupancy indicates poor perf.

Elena: +1 for arch_regex and seq thresholds. We should also consider model head size (kv dim) and kv cache footprint. For some larger kv dims even seq=64 favors big kernels on A100.

Priya: How do we detect/vet cache-state? We don't want to route mid-request but can pick at request start whether KV is present. Suggest a field: `kv_cached: true|false|unknown`. If false, prioritize minimal-launch kernels.

Sam: Good idea. Example routing table entry: `if kv_cached==false and seq<=64 -> small_fused`.

Miguel: One more wrinkle — quantization. On A100 we get good fp16 tensorcore speed; on L4 we often run int8 kernels. Need kernel_family names to imply quant mode. e.g., `triton_small_fused_int8` vs `triton_small_fused_fp16`.

Sam: Yep. Runtime should match kernel variant to model quantization. I'll add `quant` matcher.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert (weekly sweep): new default kernel selector increased p95 by ~12% on T4 for short-seq workloads. Suspect selector change from v4.2.1 -> v4.3.0. See job 2026-03-01-rt-profiles.

Priya: Oof. That explains customer reports. Let's do two things: 1) roll a canary that enforces the new small-kernel preset on T4/L4/A10 for short seqs, 2) add a retroactive eval with our dev prompt set to ensure no quality regressions.

Elena: For the canary, we should add telemetry tags (preset=small-fused, reason=canary-shortseq) so we can slice metrics. Also include `kernel_choice` in trace logs.

Miguel: I'll sketch the canary rollout: create a route rule in routing table with HT priority higher than default only for team-dev project and run for 6h. If p95 < baseline by 5% then expand. If model-decoding divergence > threshold abort.

Sam: Sounds good. Action items: Miguel -> push canary route + telemetry; Elena -> update kernel selector to include `kv_cached` and `quant` matchers; Priya -> create regression eval and schedule nightly sweep for a week. I'll synthesize the preset PR tomorrow.

Priya: Thanks. Also adding a note: capture Nsight ranges for one L4 run and one A100 run and attach next message so infra can pin time windows for NV counters.

Miguel: Will do. :thumbsup:
